scenarios.name: review-sql-injection-endpoint
scenarios.rationale: Both flag the SQL injection as critical, give the parameterized fix, and cover the async error handling, authorization and validation. B follows the rubric's structured format more closely, with severity labels, file/line, issue, fenced suggestions and a closing summary with verdict, severity counts and top fixes. A has no severity counts, no verdict and no file/line, and its findings aren't individually structured with code blocks.

scenarios.name: review-pr-diff-with-tooling-first
scenarios.rationale: Neither response reviewed the PR or ran tooling, but A at least notes the project's test/build commands and commits to running them first and to giving a severity-based verdict with the top 3 fixes, which B doesn't cover.

scenarios.name: review-react-component-uncertain-findings
scenarios.rationale: B tags confidence, acknowledges a strength, treats memoization as LOW and likely negligible (mentioning the React Compiler), and ends with a verdict and severity counts, while A omits the confidence tags, praise, and verdict, and its label fix is only partial.
